title: Enforced QA Stage
eyebrow: Design for approval, issue #264 (Enforce the QA stage) · nothing built yet

short.lead: The QA stage already exists, but nothing makes me show you the build. When I opened pull request #263 (Handover pages and checkpoints), I swapped every issue to needs review without making a QA page, so you had to ask me for one. This design makes the QA page a checkpoint, and the page builder counts each file's added and removed lines from git so the numbers are never guessed. It also fixes two problems found during that QA: an edit that got through while QA was open, and a duplicated reply.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it creates and what it needs from you.
items: QA starts when the build is handed to you
The stage becomes QA when a pull request is opened for the feature or every issue says needs review, whichever comes first. From that moment, code edits are refused.
The builder makes the QA page

make_page.py gets a QA mode. It counts each changed file's added and removed lines from git against the base branch, and shows the plan's estimate beside the count. It refuses a page with no list of what is still unverified, and if the project's style file requires pictures, it refuses a visual change that has no screenshot.
A reply can't end without it
A new row in the checkpoint table: during QA, a reply that doesn't link this feature's QA page is sent back once with the exact command to build it.
The page's Copy my reply button gives "QA passed: <feature>", or "QA failed: <feature>" followed by your list of changes.
You read the page and send one of the two replies.

changes: keep
The design loop's stages (scripts/hook.py)
Design, Plan, Build, QA and Done stay as they are.
The QA stage, the needs review label swap and the two QA replies already exist. Nothing here adds a stage or a new reply; it enforces the stage that is there.
new
QA page checkpoint (scripts/hook.py)
A blocking row in the end-of-reply checkpoint table.

It runs only while the feature is in QA. The checkpoint is met once the QA page has been built for this feature and the reply links it, either by its claude.ai link or by its docs/plans path. After that, later replies in QA pass without linking it again.
The checkpoint table checks five things: page, editor, evidence, commit and plain summary. Nothing checks for a QA page.
A sixth row, "qa page", that blocks the reply once and after that only reports, like the other five.
A build can't be handed to you without its QA page, so you never have to ask where it is.
chg
Page builder (scripts/make_page.py)
Gains a QA mode that fills in the file table itself.
The QA page's file table is typed by hand, so its counts can drift from git.
The builder fills in each file's added and removed lines from git against the base branch; the content file supplies only the plan's estimate and a plain-language note for each file.
It also refuses a QA page with no unverified list, and fixes the page's reply to "QA passed: <feature>". It records the built page in the stage file, which is how the checkpoint knows it exists.
chg
When QA starts (scripts/hook.py)
A pull request opening also starts QA.
QA starts only when every issue's label says needs review.
QA starts on that label swap or when a pull request is opened for the feature, whichever comes first.
Pull request #263 (Handover pages and checkpoints) was opened before the labels were swapped. In that gap, code edits were still allowed and no QA page was owed.
chg
The code lock in QA (scripts/hook.py)
Find out why an edit went through in QA, then fix that cause.
An Edit to templates/handover-page.html went through even though every issue of #251 (Handover pages and checkpoints) already said needs review.
The edit is reproduced in verify.py and refused, with a case that stays in the suite.

The cause is not known yet. The likeliest explanation is that the session ran plugin version 2.65.1, which kept a separate stage file for each worktree (each separate checkout of the repo). The edit then landed in a checkout whose stage file never saw the label swap. The first build step reproduces the problem before anything is changed.
chg
Writing check note (scripts/hook.py)
Asks for the corrected sentences only.
"Rewrite these and send the reply again", so you saw the whole handoff reply twice.
"Send only the corrected sentences", in the writing note and in the checkpoint table's reason line.
A Stop hook is a check that runs when I finish a reply, after you have already seen it. Blocking can't hide that reply, so only the wording can stop the repeat.
chg
Rule text and docs
One line in house-rules.md, the systems doc, and a version bump.
The rule already says that each issue's label shows whose move it is.
It also says that a build is handed over with a QA page, built by the page builder.
verify.py gains cases for the new checkpoint row, the QA mode's refusals and the reproduced QA edit.
choices: trigger
What starts QA and makes the QA page owed?
A
A pull request opening or the needs review swap, whichever comes first
Matches the wording of issue #264 (Enforce the QA stage).
B
Only the needs review swap, as today
Leaves the gap that pull request #263 (Handover pages and checkpoints) showed.
C
Only a pull request opening
A feature merged without a pull request would skip QA.
Pull request #263 (Handover pages and checkpoints) was opened before the swap. With A, the QA page would be owed from the moment it opened.
detect
How does the checkpoint know the QA page exists?
A
The builder records it in the stage file, and the reply links it
A hand-typed file can't satisfy it.
B
Any docs/plans file whose name ends -qa.html
Simpler, but a copied old QA page would pass the check.
The page check already refuses hand-written pages, and A uses the builder's mark the same way.
counts
Where do the file table's numbers come from?
A
The builder counts them from git; I write only the estimate and a note
The numbers always match git.
B
I type them; the checkpoint compares them with git
More to check, for the same result as A.
Issue #264 (Enforce the QA stage) asks for counts from git, and counting is the page builder's job, not mine.
writing
How is the duplicate reply fixed?
A
The notes ask for the corrected sentences only
One wording change in two places.
B
Make writing a blocking checkpoint
You would still see the reply first, then a second copy of it.
A Stop hook fires after the reply is shown, so B would not stop the repeat.

wrapup.summary: Make the QA page a checkpoint that the page builder satisfies, start QA when a pull request opens, fix the edit that got through during QA, and fix the duplicated reply.
wrapup.changing: In scripts/hook.py: the checkpoint table, when QA starts, the QA code lock and the writing note. Also scripts/make_page.py (the QA mode), rules/house-rules.md (one line), the systems doc for handover pages, verify.py and the plugin version.
wrapup.blocking: Your approval of this design and your answers to the four choices.
wrapup.next: A build plan page with one issue for each step, starting with the reproduction of the code-lock failure. Two things are unverified so far. First, why the edit went through during QA. Second, whether the stage file survives a cloud container being replaced, because if it doesn't, the feature would lose its stage in the middle of QA.
